payload.keyword_data: DataForSEO Google Ads, Australia, 16 Nov 2026: no volume returned for any of 24 variants (including 'honeymoon packages'), same anomaly as 15 Nov. Treat as an API gap, not zero demand. Prioritised on SERP weakness instead: page one in all three cities has no explainer.

audience.notes: Couples in their 30s, luxury, destination-minded, AUD 150K+ wedding budgets, busy careers. Fear A: spending a lot and still getting something generic (the same famous resorts, perks that turn out to be optional). Fear B: planning from the other side of the world with no one to call, and too much admin on top of the wedding (the Reddit 'exhausting' thread in the SERP). Paying parent (advisory): if family is contributing, a planner gives one booking record and one person to deal with deposits. Anti-persona: no 'cheap', 'deal' or 'free upgrades' framing; the 'is $3,000 enough' PAA is not our reader.

payload.search_intent: Mixed. Service intent (what a planner is, whether to use one, cost) versus tool intent (printable template, app). We serve the service intent and name the difference in one sentence early so tool-seekers self-select out.
payload.angle: A honeymoon planner is a specialist who designs, books and looks after the trip, not a notebook. Show what that actually covers from first call to coming home, including the invisible work nobody lists; compare it honestly with booking direct and with a general travel agent; say plainly when it is worth it and when it is not; give a short selection checklist; then show how Wedded Wonderland plans the honeymoon as one journey with the wedding. Answer the search in the first 60 words.
serp_gaps_to_win: No page in the AU top 10 explains what a honeymoon planner does. Top results are a parked domain, an off-intent destination piece, a holding page and agency homepages.
Honest 'when it is worth it, when it is not' for a luxury traveller. PAA asks about cost; nobody answers it beyond agency sales copy.
Clear comparison with booking direct and with a general travel agent on scope and fit (not pay or accreditation, which the parent owns).
The planning-a-honeymoon-while-planning-a-wedding problem (Reddit thread): one team across both.
Australian, AUD, written for couples flying long-haul from Australia.

outline.answers: The search itself, in the first 60 words, plus disambiguation.
must_include: Opening answer (under 60 words): a honeymoon planner is a travel specialist who designs your honeymoon around how you want it to feel, books flights, stays, transfers and experiences, confirms what is included in writing, and stays reachable while you travel. One short line that this is the service, not a printable planner or template.
Key takeaways block (3 to 5 specific sentences) right after the intro.
First link to /travel within 150 words, descriptive anchor (e.g. 'how our travel team plans honeymoons alongside the wedding'). Not 'honeymoon travel' as a bare anchor.
Note that people call the same role a honeymoon specialist, honeymoon travel agent or travel advisor (use the secondaries naturally).

outline.h2: What you actually get, from first call to coming home
outline.answers: What does the service include in practice? (The invisible-work H2.)
must_include: A step sequence (short numbered list or stages): a first conversation; a shortlist of two or three options with rates and inclusions; booking and payment schedule; pre-trip documents; while you travel; after you return. Brand wording for the shortlist and process only from research (live /travel 'Start planning' wording).

The invisible work, named concretely: routing and connections from Australia; transfers between stays (boat, seaplane, car) timed to check-in and check-out; matching suite categories across properties; the handover from the wedding (checkout, onward travel); noting the occasion with each property; what happens if a flight is cancelled or weather changes a transfer; someone to call while away.
Perks: say upgrades or extras are requests unless confirmed in writing for a specific booking (Fear A). No guarantees.
Do NOT include: room blocks, the brief template or the brief question list (owned by DRAFT siblings). Do NOT reproduce the inclusions list from /destination-honeymoon-packages.

outline.h2: Honeymoon planner vs booking it yourself
outline.answers: Why not just book direct with the hotel and airline?
must_include: Fair comparison: booking direct suits a single-stay, simple trip where you know the property and have time; a planner earns its place on multi-stop, long-haul, or tightly timed trips and when you are also planning a wedding.

A compact comparison table (rows: who designs the route, who handles changes and disruption, who you call while away, inclusions confirmed in writing, your time spent, cost structure). Keep cost row qualitative: 'ask how the planner is paid and whether any planning fee applies' with no figures.
Mention DIY tools exist (spreadsheets, printable planners) in one line, without linking any.

outline.h2: Honeymoon planner vs a general travel agent
outline.answers: Is a honeymoon specialist different from any travel agent?
must_include: Difference on scope and fit only: depth of knowledge of honeymoon-suited properties and suite categories, experience with the occasion, coordination with a wedding (especially a destination wedding), time given to a single trip.
Fair: many general agents are excellent; the question is whether this person has recently planned trips like yours.

One conditional link to /travel-guides/travel-advisor-wedding for how advisors are paid and accreditation (only once LIVE). Anchor must not be its keyword, e.g. 'how advisors are paid and what to check before you sign'.
Do NOT include: commission, fees detail, ATAS, ACCC consumer guarantees, 'travel advisor vs travel agent' definitions.

outline.h2: When a honeymoon planner is worth it (and when it is not)
outline.answers: PAA 'How much do honeymoon planners cost?' and the real question: is it worth it for us?
must_include: Worth it: two or more stops; remote or seaplane-access stays; tight timing straight after the wedding; a destination wedding with guests to coordinate; limited time; a milestone budget where a wrong room category hurts.
Probably not needed: one resort you already know; flexible dates; you enjoy the research.

Cost: explain that planners are paid in different ways (some by suppliers, some charge a planning fee, some both) in one or two sentences, and tell readers to ask before work starts. No figures, no USD, no claim about what anyone earns. Link the parent for detail (conditional).
Link /expert-advice/luxury-honeymoon-budget-which-destination-suits-yours (anchor e.g. 'what different budgets buy by destination').

outline.h2: What to check before you choose a honeymoon planner
outline.answers: How do we pick a good one?
must_include: Five or six selection checks: recent trips like ours (ask for examples); first-hand knowledge of the properties; clear scope in writing (what is and is not included); how payment works and in what currency; who is reachable while you are away and at what hours; whether they can work alongside a wedding planner or concierge.
One line pointing to the brief article for the full list of questions and a template (conditional on LIVE; anchor e.g. 'what to tell your planner once you have chosen one').
Fear B lives here: reachability and one point of contact.

outline.answers: How does it work with you?
must_include: Live process only (research): the 'Start planning' form on /travel, shortlist with rates and inclusions, scope can be honeymoon alone or wedding plus honeymoon; any planning fee disclosed before work starts (quote /travel wording, no figure).
Lead time from the honeymoon page wording via research (six to nine months to secure the right suite category, if research confirms).
Link /destination-honeymoon-packages with a descriptive anchor (e.g. 'what our honeymoon specialists include'). Summarise in one sentence; do not list inclusions or quote its price range.
Optional single link to /destination-packages for couples combining wedding and honeymoon at one property (anchor e.g. 'properties chosen to host a wedding, a honeymoon or both').
Soft discovery_call line linking /wonderland-concierge for couples also planning the wedding.
Closing CTA block: travel_benefits.

payload.faq_note: Six max. Q1 to Q4 from PAA (Melbourne and Brisbane). Q1: payment models in general, ask before starting, no figures. Q2: research-confirmed honeymoon page lead time; link /expert-advice/a-guide-on-when-to-go-on-honeymoon. Q3 adapts 'Is $5000 enough / realistic budget': no figures; depends on destination, length and suite; link the luxury budget article. Q4: short answer that points back to the H2s. Q5 answers the Reddit 'planning both is exhausting' intent; brand wording only. Q6 answers the related-search split (template, app, free) in two sentences. Excluded PAA: 'Is $3,000 enough' (anti-persona), 'How much does a travel agent make on a $10,000 trip?' (parent owns pay), destination list questions (off-intent).
must_include: Direct answer to 'honeymoon planner' in the first 60 words, with the service vs printable-planner distinction.
Fear A (generic result): first-hand property knowledge, suite categories, perks as requests unless confirmed in writing.
Fear B (no one to call, admin): reachability while away, one point of contact, coordinating with the wedding.
Paying parent: one booking record and clear payment schedule and currency when family contributes (one line in the checklist or the 'what you get' H2).
Invisible work named concretely in 'What you actually get'.
Honest 'when it is not worth it' paragraph.

Brand facts only from research (live /travel, /destination-honeymoon-packages, /wonderland-concierge wording) or brand-profile.md. Key takeaways block, soft discovery_call line, closing travel_benefits CTA. Australian English, AUD.
must_avoid: Reproducing the /destination-honeymoon-packages inclusions list or its price range (live page shows USD, conflicts with brand-profile).

Repeating sibling material: commission, fees detail, ATAS, ACCC, room blocks, 'who does what' table (travel-advisor-wedding); the brief template, the questions-to-ask list, the days-between-wedding-and-honeymoon section (how-to-brief).
